name: Jehiel
title: Levite and musician in the Lord's temple
summary: Jehiel was a Levite who served as a musician and gatekeeper at the ark of the covenant during King David's reign. He was among those appointed to sing praises and play instruments when the ark was brought to Jerusalem. The name Jehiel appears in several places in the Bible and refers to different individuals, but the most prominent is the Levite who served in temple worship.

keyEvents.title: Appointed as a musician at the ark of the covenant
keyEvents.description: Jehiel was appointed by David as one of the Levites to play the harp and lyres before the Lord's ark of the covenant.

keyEvents.title: Service at the ark in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Jehiel served regularly before the ark of the covenant after it was brought to Jerusalem, as part of the regular worship service.

keyEvents.title: Praise upon the arrival of the ark
keyEvents.description: When the ark arrived in Jerusalem, Jeiel participated in the great celebration of praise with cymbals, harps, and lyres.

keyEvents.title: David's arrangement of the Levites' service
keyEvents.description: King David organized the Levites' service at the sanctuary, and Jeiel was given a fixed place among the musicians who praised the Lord daily.

keyEvents.title: Jeiel mentioned in Ezra's time
keyEvents.description: Another Jeiel is mentioned among those who had taken foreign wives and who had to send them away after returning from exile in Babylon.

keyEvents.title: Jeiel in the genealogy of Benjamin
keyEvents.description: A Jeiel is named as an ancestor in the genealogy of Benjamin and as the father of Gibeon, linking him to King Saul's family.
